title: Generative OOD-regularized Model-based Policy Optimization
claim: Density estimators can misrepresent sparse regions: rollouts fall outside the training support, and a poorly fit estimator saturates instead of flagging them as OOD.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: scatter plus two histograms, shared legend below
description: The figure has three plot panels in one row. The left panel is a scatter of reward (x-axis) against action (y-axis) for a medical dataset. Points form horizontal lines at discrete action values and are colored by density with a viridis colorbar. A gray rounded box in the lower left marks the sparse region. A red dashed vertical line and a green dashed horizontal line mark thresholds. The middle panel, titled KDE Distributions, is a histogram of log-likelihoods. Purple transition-rollout mass piles into one tall spike at about -25. The orange training distribution is a bump near 0. The right panel, titled NeuralODE Distributions, is a similar histogram. Its purple rollouts spread smoothly over a wide negative range, while the orange training mass is concentrated at 0. A shared legend sits below the histograms. The eye goes first to the tall purple spike in the KDE panel.
caption: Left: reward–action space of the medical dataset, with the sparse region in gray. Right: transition rollout and training distributions modeled by KDE and NeuralODE. Rollouts with low likelihoods indicate OOD behavior, while KDE saturates with a large spike.
abstract: We study sequential decision-making with offline reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional offline RL policies may result in out-of-distribution (OOD) actions when training relies only on sparse offline representations. To ensure safe offline policies in a sparse state-action space, we explore how density estimation models can be integrated into model-based RL methods to avoid OOD regions. Generative models are capable of explicitly modeling the density in sparse state-action spaces. Building on this, we introduce Generative OOD-regularized Model-based Policy Optimization (GORMPO), a density-regularized offline RL algorithm that uses generative density modeling to restrict policy updates to high-density areas of the dataset. Furthermore, we examine whether better OOD detection corresponds to better model-based offline policies. We compare (1) the OOD detection capabilities of various density estimators and (2) their performance within the GORMPO framework on a real-world medical dataset and sparse offline RL datasets. We provide theoretical guarantees bounding GORMPO's performance gap in terms of density estimation error, ensuring near-optimal policies under imperfect density estimates. Empirically, GORMPO remains competitive in reward and improves clinical metrics compared to state-of-the-art clinical RL models, and outperforms state-of-the-art offline RL models in offline RL benchmarks. Our empirical findings show that better OOD detection generally results in improved policies in environments with stable dynamics, while conservative penalties with poor density estimation are favored when dynamics are uncertain. Code, checkpoints, sparse, and OOD D4RL datasets are available at https://github.com/Rose-STL-Lab/GORMPO.
